name: CEILING
description: CEILING rounds a number up, away from zero, to the nearest multiple of a specified significance.
tldr: Rounds a number up to the nearest multiple of significance.

parameters.name: number
parameters.description: The value you want to round.

parameters.name: significance
parameters.description: The multiple to which you want to round. In classic CEILING, number and significance should share the same sign.

basicExample.description: Round a price up to the nearest 5 cents
basicExample.explanation: 4.45 is the first multiple of 0.05 that is greater than or equal to 4.42.

advancedExamples.title: Round up to the next ten
advancedExamples.description: Round 123 up to a multiple of 10.
advancedExamples.explanation: 130 is the next multiple of 10 at or above 123.

advancedExamples.title: Negative numbers round toward zero
advancedExamples.description: CEILING rounds toward positive infinity, so negatives move toward zero.
advancedExamples.explanation: The smallest multiple of 1 that is ≥ -4.3 is -4.

howItWorks: CEILING finds the smallest multiple of significance that is greater than or equal to number (rounding toward positive infinity). In the classic version, if number is positive and significance is negative, Excel returns #NUM!; use CEILING.MATH to lift that restriction.

howToSteps.name: Select the cell
howToSteps.text: Click the cell for the result.

limitations: If number is positive and significance is negative, classic CEILING returns #NUM! (CEILING.MATH does not).
CEILING rounds toward positive infinity, so negative numbers move toward zero, which can surprise users expecting 'more negative' rounding.
A significance of 0 returns 0 rather than an error.

commonErrors.cause: Number is positive while significance is negative (classic CEILING).
commonErrors.fix: Make the signs match, or switch to CEILING.MATH.
Use numeric values or numeric cell references.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: Google Sheets supports CEILING with the same syntax and behavior.

faq.question: What is the difference between CEILING and CEILING.MATH?
faq.answer: CEILING.MATH (Excel 2013+) allows any sign combination and adds a mode argument for controlling negative rounding; classic CEILING is stricter about signs.

faq.question: Does CEILING round away from zero?
faq.answer: It rounds toward positive infinity, so positives go up and negatives go toward zero (e.g. CEILING(-4.3,1) = -4).
